'''Daniel Hiram''' "'''Boobie'''" '''Gibson''' (born February 27, 1986)<ref name=nbabio>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121202050613/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/daniel_gibson/bio.html NBA.com: Daniel Gibson Bio Page]</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was selected by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the second round of the [[2006 NBA draft]] and played seven seasons for them.

==Early life==
Gibson averaged 25.5 points per game and 9.3 assists per game while leading [[Jesse H. Jones High School|Jones High School]] in [[Houston, Texas]] to a 31–4 record and the Texas Class 4A state title as a senior. It marked the school's first state championship since 1965. Gibson graduated sixth out of 212 students in his high school class, and was a member of the National Honor Society.<ref>[http://hs.houstonisd.org/JonesHS/alumni.htm HoustonISD.org Jones HS Alumni] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070609143108/http://hs.houstonisd.org/JonesHS/alumni.htm |date=June 9, 2007 }}</ref>

==College career==
Gibson starred as a guard in [[college basketball]] the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. In his two seasons with the [[Texas Longhorns|Longhorns]], he scored 935 points, including 175 [[three-point field goal]]s. Gibson made 101 threes during the 2005–2006 season, including 9 of 12 against the [[Baylor Bears]] on January 21, 2006. It was one short of the Texas record of 10 set by Al Coleman against [[Kansas State University|Kansas State]] in January 1997.<ref name=ninethrees>[http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=260210239 No. 6 Texas trounces Baylor behind Gibson's 37] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305073511/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=260210239 |date=March 5, 2016 }}</ref> He scored a personal-high 37 points in that same game.<ref name=ninethrees/>

Gibson played two seasons at Texas and averaged 13.8 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 68 games (all starts). He was named Honorable Mention All-America by The Associated Press following his sophomore season. Gibson averaged 13.4 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game as a sophomore. He earned First-Team NABC All-District 9 honors and was named All-Big 12 Third Team. He set a school record for most three-point field goals made in a season (101). He was one of 16 finalists for the Bob Cousy Award, given to the nation's top point guard. He sank at least four three-pointers in a game on 10 occasions. Gibson was named the Big 12 Freshman of the Year after his first season, averaging 14.2 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game. He was also named All-Big 12 Third Team and became the first freshman in school history to lead Texas in scoring.<ref name=nbabio/>
On June 7, 2006, Gibson announced his decision to forgo his two remaining years of college eligibility and enter the [[NBA draft]].

==NBA career==
===Cleveland Cavaliers===
====2006–07 season and NBA Finals vs San Antonio Spurs====
On June 29, 2006, Gibson was drafted in the second round with the 42nd overall pick of the [[1967 NBA Draft|NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. After a May 2006 pre-draft workout with the Cavs, Gibson canceled his remaining workouts with other teams and refused to work out for any other team before the draft. It is believed this was the reason Gibson fell to the second round after some thought he might be drafted in the first round.<ref>{{cite news | last = Windhorst | first = Brian | url = http://www.topix.net/content/kri/2043470263221778260707634919040687435312 | title = Let's play Match Game | work = [[Akron Beacon Journal]] | date = December 11, 2006 | access-date = July 19, 2007 }} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref> He joined a Cavaliers backcourt that was the worst in the league in scoring the previous season.

In his rookie season, Gibson averaged 4.6 points per game and led all rookies in three-point field goal percentage, shooting 41.9%. Daniel contributed in helping the Cleveland Cavaliers reach the NBA playoffs. Cavs coach [[Mike Brown (basketball coach)|Mike Brown]] gave Gibson his first place in the starting line-up on December 6, 2006, against the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20061206/TORCLE/boxscore.html nba.com boxscore] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115134124/http://www.nba.com/games/20061206/TORCLE/boxscore.html |date=January 15, 2016 }}</ref> He finished the game with 18 points, 5 rebounds, and 2 assists.   Overall, Gibson started 16 games and averaged 8.8 points on 53.9% shooting in his starts.

Gibson had his first big playoff opportunity in game 3 of the 2007 Eastern Conference Finals against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He scored 9 points, including two three-pointers. He also grabbed 2 rebounds, blocked 1 shot, and had an important steal from [[Tayshaun Prince]] late in the fourth quarter. He followed this in game 4, scoring 21 points, which came from only 6 field goal attempts. Gibson was also 12 of 12 from the free throw line. In Game 6, Gibson scored a career-high 31 points, sending the Cavaliers to their first NBA Finals.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270602005|title=Gibson's 31 points, James' balanced play puts Cavs in NBA Finals|website=ESPN|date=June 2, 2007|access-date=December 11, 2016|agency=Associated Press|archive-date=December 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220122139/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270602005|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Gibson was mentored in defensive skills by veteran teammate [[Eric Snow]] in the 2006–07 season.

In game one of the 2007 NBA Finals against the Spurs, Gibson shined off the bench, leading the team in scoring with Gibson scoring 16 points efficiently, on 7 of 9 shooting. The Cavs would go on to lose game one, however, 76–85.

In game two of the NBA Finals, Gibson score 15 points and overall being the second leading scorer behind LeBron.

His first start in the playoffs came in the third game of the [[2007 NBA Finals]], after an injury to [[Larry Hughes]]. Game 3 was one of Gibson’s worst performances of the entire playoffs. He shot just 1 for 10, and 0 for 5 from three. Shots could not fall, and the Cavaliers fell 0-3 in the series. He would start the following Game 4 as well.

In the final Game 4 of the 2007 NBA Finals, Daniel Gibson had a decent game, dropping 10 points to an eventual loss to the San Antonio Spurs. The series would be a sweep. He shot 4–10 from the field, and 2 for 6 from three. Daniel Gibson averaged 0 turnovers for the entire finals, and was the third leading scorer for the Cavaliers at 10.8 points per game behind Drew Gooden at 12.8 points a game. However, Daniel Gibson struggled defensively guarding Tony Parker who averaged 24.5 points a game and a finals MVP Trophy.

====2007–08 season====
[[File:GibsonCavs.jpg|thumb|upright|Gibson with the Cavaliers]]
Gibson played in 58 games, starting 26 of those. He averaged 10.4 points, 2.5 assists and 2.3 rebounds per game. He scored a season-high 26 points on November 20, 2007, against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. Gibson had a career-high six three-pointers against the [[New York Knicks]] on November 2, 2007, and a career-high eight assists against the [[Washington Wizards]] on December 5, 2007. Gibson ranked fifth in the NBA in three-point shooting percentage, making 44.0% of his three-point attempts.<ref name=career_stats>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/daniel_gibson/career_stats.html NBA.com : Daniel Gibson Career Stats Page<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228005840/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/daniel_gibson/career_stats.html |date=December 28, 2014 }}</ref>  Gibson missed 18 games in February and March due to an ankle injury suffered when he and the [[Indiana Pacers]]' [[Travis Diener]] dove in the lane for a loose ball in the second quarter of a Cavs win over the Pacers.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=3257970 Cavaliers Daniel Gibson could miss 6 weeks with ankle sprain]</ref>  He returned to action on March 29, 2008, against the [[Detroit Pistons]], scoring only 1 point in 18 minutes.<ref>[http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280329008 With Nets loss, Cavs clinch playoff spot despite loss to Pistons] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303175421/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280329008 |date=March 3, 2016 }}</ref>

In game 5 against the [[Boston Celtics]], in the Eastern Conference Semi-Finals, Gibson separated his shoulder and missed the final two games;<ref name=anklesurgery/><ref name=fiveyeardeal>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3491666 Cavs commit to Gibson with new five-year contract]</ref> the Cavaliers lost 4–3 in the series. Gibson said missing game 7 of the Boston series still haunts him: "I've had a lot of sleepless nights just wondering where I could have helped the team."<ref name=fiveyeardeal/>

Gibson was selected to participate in the [[Rookie Challenge]] (Sophomore team)<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/allstar2008/news/story?id=3222734 Blazers' Roy, Sonics' Durant lead Sophomores and Rookies]</ref> and the [[Three-point Shootout]] during the [[2008 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|2008 NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[New Orleans, Louisiana|New Orleans]].

During the first half of the Rookie Challenge, Gibson tied the record for total three-pointers made, despite not being a starter in the game.  He later set the record in the second half with eleven total three-pointers, finishing the game shooting 11–20 from beyond the three-point line. Gibson was named MVP of the game, finishing with 33 points, 4 rebounds, 2 assists, and 2 steals.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/allstar2008/news/story?id=3248607 Cavs' Gibson sinks record 11 3-pointers in blowout vs. rookies]</ref>

Gibson finished in second place in the [[Three-point Shootout]]. He advanced to the final round by scoring 17 points in the first round, which tied him with [[Dirk Nowitzki]] for second place. In the final round, Gibson again scored 17 points, but it was not enough. Defending champion [[Jason Kapono]] tied the 22-year shootout record of 25 points for the victory.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/allstar2008/news/story?id=3249672 Howard proves big men can fly, earns dunk title]</ref>

====2008–09 season====
On June 10, 2008, Gibson had surgery on his ankle in Houston.<ref name=anklesurgery>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3436302 Gibson has ankle surgery, expected to be ready for training camp]</ref> On July 16, 2008, the Cavaliers signed Gibson to a five-year, $21 million contract.<ref>[http://www.news-herald.com/articles/2008/07/20/local%20sports/19862031.txt Gibson signs five year deal] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130805170107/http://www.news-herald.com/articles/2008/07/20/local%20sports/19862031.txt |date=August 5, 2013 }}</ref>

On November 26, 2008, Gibson scored his 1,000th career point in the Cavs' game against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120720224502/http://www.basketball-reference.com/fc/pgl.cgi?player=gibsoda01&year=2009|title=Daniel Gibson Game Log}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gibson is the son of Byron and Cheryl Gibson. His father played basketball for the University of Houston.<ref name=nbabio/> Gibson and his ex-wife, [[Keyshia Cole]], have a son.<ref name=nbabio/> The couple's 2011 wedding was filmed and aired on their [[Black Entertainment Television|BET]] reality TV series ''[[Keyshia & Daniel: Family First]]'' on October 9, 2012.<ref>{{cite web |last=Penn |first=Charli |url=http://www.essence.com/2012/10/09/making-it-work-keyshia-cole-and-daniel-gibson-why-they-chose-each-other |title=Making It Work: Keyshia Cole and Daniel Gibson On Why They Chose Each Other |work=Essence.com |date=October 9, 2012 |access-date=November 22, 2015 |archive-date=November 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151123140720/http://www.essence.com/2012/10/09/making-it-work-keyshia-cole-and-daniel-gibson-why-they-chose-each-other |url-status=live }}</ref> The couple later separated in 2014.

On July 29, 2013, Gibson turned himself in to New Orleans police to face a charge of second degree battery related to an incident that took place earlier that month. His attorney declined to comment on the matter, but police said Gibson struck a man, breaking his jaw, in an altercation at a local night club.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2013/news/07/29/free-agent-gibson-battery-charge.ap/ Free agent Gibson faces battery charge] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222125823/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/07/29/free-agent-gibson-battery-charge.ap/ |date=February 22, 2016 }}</ref>

After the 2012–2013 season, injuries to his foot and ankle, grieving his grandmother's death, and a lengthy divorce, Gibson began suffering from depression and anxiety, and began writing music to cope with the issues, contrary to rumors that he intentionally was starting a rap career.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uproxx.com/dimemag/daniel-gibson-interview-cleveland-cavaliers-lebron-james/|title=Former Cavs G Daniel Gibson Contemplated Suicide After Career Ended|last=Maroney|first=Oliver|date=May 18, 2017|website=UPROXX|access-date=January 3, 2019|archive-date=January 3, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103110306/https://uproxx.com/dimemag/daniel-gibson-interview-cleveland-cavaliers-lebron-james/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2017, he toured internationally with other retired NBA players as a part of the Champions Basketball League <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theringer.com/sports/2017/8/23/16184910/champions-basketball-league-launch-delay|title=The Champions Basketball League Could Be a Utopian Pro Sports Alternative—If It Ever Happens|last=Rosen|first=Sam|date=August 23, 2017|website=The Ringer|access-date=January 3, 2019|archive-date=January 3, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103110550/https://www.theringer.com/sports/2017/8/23/16184910/champions-basketball-league-launch-delay|url-status=live}}</ref> and he and Cole were featured in the VH1 reality TV show ''[[Love & Hip Hop: Hollywood]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.essence.com/celebrity/black-celeb-couples/keyshia-cole-husband-daniel-gibson-love-hip-hop-hollywood|title=Keyshia Cole and Estranged Husband Attempt to Rebuild Their Relationship on 'Love & Hip Hop Hollywood'|access-date=October 24, 2017|archive-date=October 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024100854/https://www.essence.com/celebrity/black-celeb-couples/keyshia-cole-husband-daniel-gibson-love-hip-hop-hollywood|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2018, Gibson was on the MTV television show ''[[The Challenge: Champs vs. Stars (season 2)|The Challenge: Champs vs. Stars]]''.

On December 10, 2025, Gibson was arrested during a traffic stop. He was pulled over by [[Beachwood, Ohio|Beachwood]] police for driving a pickup truck with no tail lights. He had an active warrant out of Mansfield Municipal Court for failing to appear in court on a speeding ticket issued by the [[Ohio State Highway Patrol]] from 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Thyret |first1=Julia |title=Former Cavs player arrested for failing to appear in court on a speeding ticket |url=https://www.cleveland19.com/2025/12/10/former-cavs-player-arrested-failing-appear-court-speeding-ticket/ |website=www.cleveland19.com |access-date=12 December 2025 |language=en |date=10 December 2025}}</ref>
